answer: The maximum amount of the buy-back is 25% or less of the aggregate of paid-up capital and free reserves of the company. With paid-up capital and free reserves of ₹500 crore, the maximum buy-back amount is 25% * ₹500 crore = ₹125 crore (or less). The maximum total debt (aggregate of secured and unsecured debts) the company can carry after the buy-back must be in a ratio of less than or equal to 2:1 to the paid-up capital and free reserves after the buy-back. Specifically, the maximum debt allowed after the buy-back is 2 * (Paid-up Capital and Free Reserves after buy-back). Since the maximum buy-back is 25% (₹125 crore), the remaining paid-up capital and free reserves after the buy-back is at least ₹500 crore - ₹125 crore = ₹375 crore, making the maximum total debt 2 * ₹375 crore = ₹750 crore (or up to 2 * ₹500 crore = ₹1000 crore depending on the exact buy-back amount utilized).
